gulas.opis: The best-known Gorski kotar dish: venison, red deer, wild boar or bear, slowly cooked with onion and red wine. Served with polenta, potato gnocchi or homemade bread.
gulas.probaj: In Fužine, Hotel Bitoraj, Konoba Volta and Lovački dom Arnika are known for goulash; it's also served in other restaurants and mountain huts with home cooking.

suho.opis: A cold starter: cured bear, boar or deer meat with škripavac (squeaky cheese) and homemade bread.
suho.probaj: As a starter in restaurants; cured meats also from small local producers.

pastrva.opis: The most prized fish of the local rivers and lakes. Baked, grilled or cooked in a thick fish soup.
pastrva.probaj: Restaurants by the Kupa, the Kupica and the lakes.

zabe.opis: An old Gorski kotar speciality: breaded, or stewed in a sauce with snails and mushrooms.

puh.opis: A dish of the old Gorani: dormouse roasted or as a goulash. It was valued for its meat and fat, and dormouse hunting is still a local tradition.
puh.probaj: Rarely on the menu; mostly at local dormouse evenings.

nadjev.opis: An Easter dish: pork stomach stuffed with cubes of bread, ham, bacon, spring onion and eggs, then boiled or lightly smoked.
nadjev.probaj: In homes and on Easter tables.

zelje.opis: Once the main winter dish, now a side: sauerkraut with garlic, sausage or blood sausage.

gljive.opis: Porcini, chanterelles, morels and parasols: as a main dish, in a sauce or with meat. In winter eaten dried or pickled.
gljive.probaj: Restaurants in season. Before picking, check the species in the Gljive Hrvatske app.

strudla.opis: A Gorski kotar dessert: thin pastry with wild blueberries, sugar and cinnamon, served warm and dusted with icing sugar. Apple and cheese strudels are made too.
strudla.kad: all year, best in summer when blueberries ripen
strudla.probaj: Hotel Bitoraj in Fužine is known for it; also in other restaurants.

rakije.opis: Homemade plum, apple and pear brandy and juniper brandy (brinjevec). Liqueurs and juices from blueberries, strawberries, raspberries and blackberries, and lately Gorski kotar gin.
rakije.probaj: At family farms and in restaurants; see the Farms & local filter.

lynx.ime: The Risnjak mountain probably got its name from me – the lynx (ris in Croatian). The national park has existed since 1949.
lynx.povratak: Lynx disappeared from these forests in the early 20th century. In 1973, six lynx from Slovakia were brought to the Slovenian part of the Dinaric mountains – today's lynx here are their descendants.
lynx.geni: All Dinaric lynx descend from only six animals, so we are too closely related. That's why the LIFE Lynx project is bringing lynx from the Carpathians to the Dinarides.
lynx.zastita: In Croatia I'm a strictly protected species. Hunting lynx has been banned since 1998.
lynx.teritorij: I'm a loner. A male's territory covers 120 to 1800 km² – even the smallest is bigger than the whole of Risnjak National Park.
lynx.plijen: I mostly hunt roe deer. An adult male weighs 18 to 25 kg, a female 12 to 16 kg.
lynx.zvijeri: All three large carnivores live in Gorski kotar: the bear, the wolf and me. Zelenko the bear and I are neighbours!
